title: PC in VLAN 10 Cannot Reach Server in VLAN 30
symptoms: PC receives an IP address but cannot reach the server in VLAN 30. The PC can ping its default gateway (192.168.10.1). Pinging 192.168.30.10 results in timeout.
topology_notes: PC is connected to access switch SW1 (port Fa0/1, access VLAN 10). SW1 connects to router R1 via trunk link (Gi0/0). Server is in VLAN 30 connected to SW1 (port Fa0/24). R1 has subinterfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 but VLAN 30 is missing.

show_commands.output:
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/0       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/0       1-29,31-4094

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/0       1,10,20

VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    
10   STUDENT                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20   FACULTY                          active    Fa0/3, Fa0/4
30   SERVER                           active    Fa0/24

Codes: C - connected, L - local

      192.168.10.0/24 is variably subnetted
C     192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
L     192.168.10.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
      192.168.20.0/24 is variably subnetted
C     192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20

expected_fault: Router subinterface for VLAN 30 is missing. VLAN 30 also not in trunk allowed list.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Router subinterface for VLAN 30 (GigabitEthernet0/0.30) is missing on R1. Additionally, VLAN 30 is excluded from the trunk allowed VLAN list (vlans 1-29,31-4094).
evidence: show ip route: No route for 192.168.30.0/24 network
show interfaces trunk: VLAN 30 excluded from trunk (vlans 1-29,31-4094)
show vlan brief: VLAN 30 SERVER exists on switch
fix_steps: Add VLAN 30 to trunk: SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30

checks.message: VLAN 30 excluded from trunk allowed list

human_review.explanation: AI correctly identified both the trunk exclusion and missing subinterface on the router.

title: Native VLAN Mismatch on Inter-Switch Trunk
symptoms: CDP error logs flooding switch console: %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (1) with SW2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (99). Management traffic dropping.
topology_notes: SW1 connects to SW2 over 802.1Q trunk on Gi0/1. SW1 has default native VLAN 1, while SW2 was configured with native VLAN 99.

show_commands.output:
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Name: Gi0/1
Administrative Mode: trunk
Operational Mode: trunk
Trunking Native Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch: SW1 has Native VLAN 1 whereas SW2 has Native VLAN 99.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: 802.1Q Native VLAN mismatch between SW1 (VLAN 1) and SW2 (VLAN 99) on trunk link Gi0/1. Untagged frames will leak between different VLANs causing spanning-tree loops and packet drops.
evidence: CDP syslog reports Native VLAN mismatch (1 vs 99)
show interfaces trunk shows Native VLAN 1 on SW1
fix_steps: Align native VLAN on SW1: SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk native vlan 99
Verify CDP warnings clear: show cdp neighbors detail

human_review.explanation: Accurate diagnosis. Matching Native VLAN 99 on both trunk endpoints resolves CDP errors.

title: Access Port Assigned to Default VLAN 1 Instead of Finance VLAN 20
symptoms: Finance user cannot connect to accounting software or print to Finance printer. PC receives 169.254.x.x APIPA address.
topology_notes: Finance PC is plugged into switch SW1 port Fa0/5. Finance VLAN is 20 with DHCP server on 192.168.20.1.

show_commands.output:
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/5, Fa0/6, Fa0/7
10   STUDENT                          active    Fa0/1, Fa0/2
20   FINANCE                          active    Fa0/3, Fa0/4

expected_fault: Port Fa0/5 is in VLAN 1 (default) instead of VLAN 20 FINANCE.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Switch port Fa0/5 is assigned to default VLAN 1 rather than Finance VLAN 20. DHCP discover broadcasts cannot reach the VLAN 20 DHCP server.
evidence: show vlan brief shows Fa0/5 active in VLAN 1
VLAN 20 exists with ports Fa0/3, Fa0/4 only

human_review.explanation: Straightforward access VLAN misconfiguration.

title: VTP Pruning Stripping VLAN 50 Across Distribution Trunk
symptoms: Hosts on SW-Access2 in VLAN 50 cannot communicate with central servers. VTP is operating in Server/Client mode across the campus.
topology_notes: SW-Dist1 is VTP server with pruning enabled. SW-Access2 had no active access ports in VLAN 50 initially, causing VTP pruning on the uplink. A new host was just plugged in.

show_commands.output:
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned
Gi0/1       1,10,20,30

VTP Version                     : 2
Configuration Revision          : 14
Maximum VLANs supported locally : 255
VTP Operating Mode              : Server
VTP Domain Name                 : CAMPUS
VTP Pruning Mode                : Enabled

expected_fault: VLAN 50 is pruned on the trunk because access switch reported no active ports in VLAN 50.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: VTP domain name is mismatched between switches or VTP password was typed incorrectly, preventing VLAN 50 database propagation.
evidence: VLAN 50 missing from trunk active list
fix_steps: Reset VTP domain name: SW1(config)# vtp domain CAMPUS
Set VTP mode to transparent: SW1(config)# vtp mode transparent

corrected_response.root_cause: VTP Pruning is enabled globally and dynamically pruned VLAN 50 from trunk Gi0/1 because SW-Access2 did not have an active access port in VLAN 50. The VTP domain and revision are actually fine.
fix_steps: Verify VLAN 50 exists on SW-Access2: show vlan brief
Assign user port to VLAN 50 to trigger VTP join: switchport access vlan 50
Or clear pruning for VLAN 50: switchport trunk pruning vlan remove 50
Verify forwarding state: show interfaces Gi0/1 trunk

human_review.explanation: AI MISDIAGNOSIS (Responsible AI): AI claimed VTP domain name mismatch. The show vtp status clearly confirms VTP Server with domain CAMPUS is working normally. The actual root cause is dynamic VTP Pruning on the trunk.

title: Gateway Unreachable — Subnet Mask Mismatch (/24 vs /28)
symptoms: PC cannot reach the Internet or any device outside the local switch. Pinging default gateway 192.168.1.1 returns "Destination host unreachable".

show_commands.output:
Interface                  IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0         192.168.1.1     YES manual up                    up

interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
 duplex auto
 speed auto

expected_fault: PC is configured with /28 mask (192.168.1.16 - 192.168.1.31) making 192.168.1.1 appear in a different subnet.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch between PC and Router. PC has 255.255.255.240 (/28), placing host .30 in subnet 192.168.1.16/28, while Gateway .1 is in 192.168.1.0/28. The PC attempts to ARP through a gateway it cannot reach.

human_review.explanation: Verified. Changing PC subnet mask to 255.255.255.0 restored gateway reachability immediately.

title: HSRP Split Brain — ACL Blocking UDP 1985 Hellos
symptoms: Both R1 and R2 are in HSRP "Active" state simultaneously on VLAN 10 (Virtual IP 192.168.10.254). Duplicate MAC address warnings on LAN switches.
topology_notes: R1 and R2 participate in HSRP group 10 on interface Gi0/0.10. An access-list was recently applied on R2 GigabitEthernet0/0.10.

show_commands.output:
P indicates configured to preempt.
                     |
Interface   Grp  Pri P State   Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gi0/0.10    10   110 P Active  local           unknown         192.168.10.254

Extended IP access list 100
    10 permit tcp any any eq 80
    20 permit tcp any any eq 443
    30 deny ip any any (142 matches)

expected_fault: ACL 100 inbound on R2 subinterface denies HSRP UDP port 1985 multicast packets (224.0.0.2).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: HSRP Group number mismatch between R1 and R2 or HSRP priority conflict.
fix_steps: Change HSRP priority on R2: standby 10 priority 90

checks.message: ACL contains deny statement with active matches

corrected_response.root_cause: Extended ACL 100 applied inbound on R2 Gi0/0.10 lacks a permit rule for HSRP multicast traffic (UDP port 1985 to 224.0.0.2 / 224.0.0.102). R2 never hears R1 hellos and enters Active state.
fix_steps: Add HSRP permit rule to ACL 100: R2(config)# ip access-list extended 100
R2(config-ext-nacl)# 25 permit udp any host 224.0.0.2 eq 1985
R2(config-ext-nacl)# 26 permit udp any host 224.0.0.102 eq 1985
Verify HSRP state converges: R2# show standby brief

human_review.explanation: AI MISDIAGNOSIS (Responsible AI): AI guessed HSRP group mismatch, failing to correlate the ACL 100 deny matches on the interface. Adding UDP 1985 permit statement immediately resolved the dual-active state.

title: Proxy ARP Disabled on Gateway Router Interface
symptoms: Legacy client configured without a default gateway fails to communicate outside the subnet. "no ip proxy-arp" was applied during security hardening.
topology_notes: Host A (192.168.1.50/24) has no default gateway configured, relying on Proxy ARP from Router R1 (192.168.1.1).

show_commands.output:
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet address is 192.168.1.1/24
  Broadcast address is 255.255.255.255
  Proxy ARP is disabled

expected_fault: Proxy ARP is disabled on Gi0/0, preventing unconfigured legacy clients from resolving remote IPs.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Proxy ARP is disabled on router interface Gi0/0. Legacy devices configured without an explicit default gateway cannot resolve MAC addresses for remote destinations.
evidence: show ip interface Gi0/0 confirms Proxy ARP is disabled
fix_steps: Best Practice: Configure explicit default gateway 192.168.1.1 on Host A
Or temporarily re-enable Proxy ARP: R1(config-if)# ip proxy-arp

human_review.explanation: Configuring default gateway on Host A is the proper permanent solution.

title: DHCP Pool Exhaustion in Engineering Subnet
symptoms: New laptops joining VLAN 20 cannot acquire IP addresses. Existing devices retain communication until lease expiration.
topology_notes: DHCP pool POOL_ENG configured with 192.168.20.0/24. 253 addresses leased.

show_commands.output:
Pool POOL_ENG :
 Total addresses                 : 254
 Leased addresses                : 254
 Excluded addresses              : 0
 Pending event                   : none
 1 subnet is currently in the subnet list
 network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0

IP address        Detection method   Detection time
-- No conflicts --

expected_fault: DHCP pool POOL_ENG is 100% utilized (254 of 254 leased).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: DHCP address pool POOL_ENG on R1 is completely exhausted (254/254 active leases). No free IP addresses remain for new clients.
evidence: show ip dhcp pool shows Leased addresses: 254 out of 254
fix_steps: Clear inactive leases: clear ip dhcp binding *
Reduce lease duration: R1(config-dhcp)# lease 0 8 0 (8 hours)
Expand subnet mask from /24 to /23 or configure secondary pool

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Reduced lease time to 4 hours and cleared old bindings.

title: Missing IP Helper-Address for Remote DHCP Relay
symptoms: Clients in VLAN 30 fail to receive DHCP leases. Central DHCP server 10.0.0.5 shows zero DHCP discover requests received from 192.168.30.0 subnet.
topology_notes: VLAN 30 gateway resides on Router R1 subinterface Gi0/0.30 (192.168.30.1). DHCP server is located across the WAN on 10.0.0.5.

show_commands.output:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30
 ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0

expected_fault: Subinterface Gi0/0.30 is missing "ip helper-address 10.0.0.5".

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: Central DHCP server service has stopped or firewall is blocking UDP port 67/68 across the WAN.
fix_steps: Restart DHCP service on Windows/Linux server

checks.message: DHCP relay not confirmed — verify ip helper-address

corrected_response.root_cause: Router R1 subinterface Gi0/0.30 lacks "ip helper-address 10.0.0.5". Client broadcast DISCOVER packets are dropped at the router rather than being unicast forwarded to the DHCP server.

human_review.explanation: AI REJECTION (Responsible AI): AI hallucinated server crash and WAN firewall blocks. The running config clearly shows Gi0/0.30 has no ip helper-address configured.

title: DHCP Snooping Untrusted Uplink Dropping DHCP Offers
symptoms: DHCP Snooping enabled on SW1. All clients stopped getting IP addresses immediately after feature activation. Console logs: %DHCP_SNOOPING-5-DHCP_OFFER_DROPPED.
topology_notes: SW1 Gi0/1 is the uplink to the Core Switch where DHCP server is connected. DHCP Snooping is enabled on VLAN 10,20.

show_commands.output:
Switch DHCP snooping is enabled
DHCP snooping is configured on following VLANs:
10,20
Insertion of option 82 is enabled

Interface                  Trusted    Rate limit (pps)
------------------------   -------    ----------------

expected_fault: Uplink port Gi0/1 is not configured as trusted (ip dhcp snooping trust).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: DHCP Snooping is enabled on SW1, but uplink interface Gi0/1 is untrusted. DHCP Snooping drops all server responses (DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK) arriving on untrusted ports.
evidence: show ip dhcp snooping shows 0 trusted interfaces

human_review.explanation: Accurate diagnosis. Uplink must be trusted for DHCP Snooping to permit server responses.

title: DNS Resolution Failing — Client DNS IP Set to Non-Existent Host
symptoms: Users can ping external IPs (8.8.8.8) but cannot browse websites by name (e.g. www.cisco.com fails). nslookup times out after 2 seconds.
topology_notes: LAN subnet 192.168.1.0/24. Actual DNS server is 192.168.1.10. PC static configuration has DNS set to 192.168.1.254 (non-existent).

show_commands.output:
ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL
 network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.1.1
 dns-server 192.168.1.254

expected_fault: DHCP pool configures DNS server as 192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.10.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: DHCP pool LAN_POOL on router advertises invalid DNS server 192.168.1.254. Hosts cannot resolve domain names despite valid IP routing to external destinations.

human_review.explanation: Updated DHCP pool dns-server parameter. Name resolution restored.

title: Router CLI Hangs on Mistyped Commands (Domain Lookup Timeout)
symptoms: Whenever engineer mistypes a command in privilege exec mode, console freezes for 30 seconds with "Translating mistyped_command... domain server (255.255.255.255)".
topology_notes: Lab router R1 has default "ip domain-lookup" enabled without a valid DNS server configured.

show_commands.output: ip domain-lookup

expected_fault: Default "ip domain-lookup" enabled on router without nameserver.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Router interprets mistyped CLI inputs as hostnames and sends broadcast DNS queries to 255.255.255.255, hanging the terminal until timeout occurs.

human_review.explanation: Standard Cisco best practice for console management.

title: Static Route Missing — Branch Cannot Reach HQ Subnet
symptoms: Branch PC cannot ping HQ server. Branch router R2 has default route to ISP, but HQ LAN 10.1.0.0/24 is not reachable.
topology_notes: Branch R2 connects to HQ R1 over point-to-point WAN 203.0.113.0/30. R1 is 203.0.113.1, R2 is 203.0.113.2.

show_commands.output:
Gateway of last resort is 198.51.100.1 to network 0.0.0.0

S*    0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 198.51.100.1
      203.0.113.0/30 is subnetted, 1 subnets
C        203.0.113.0 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
      10.2.0.0/24 is subnetted, 1 subnets
C        10.2.0.0 is directly connected, FastEthernet0/0

expected_fault: Missing static route for 10.1.0.0/24 on R2 AND return route on R1.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: Static route for 10.1.0.0/24 is missing on R2. Default route forwards private packets to ISP.
evidence: No route for 10.1.0.0/24 in show ip route
fix_steps: Add static route on R2: R2(config)# ip route 10.1.0.0 255.255.255.0 203.0.113.1

corrected_response.root_cause: Static route for 10.1.0.0/24 is missing on R2, AND return route for 10.2.0.0/24 is missing on HQ router R1. Routing must be bidirectional.
fix_steps: Add route on Branch: R2(config)# ip route 10.1.0.0 255.255.255.0 203.0.113.1
Add return route on HQ: R1(config)# ip route 10.2.0.0 255.255.255.0 203.0.113.2

human_review.explanation: AI MISDIAGNOSIS (Responsible AI): AI identified only the forward route on R2 and missed the return route on R1. Both routes are strictly necessary for end-to-end communication.

title: Floating Static Route Administrative Distance Conflict
symptoms: Backup link is taking priority over OSPF primary route. Traffic unnecessarily traversing costly metered cellular backup.
topology_notes: Primary link uses OSPF (AD 110). Backup static route was mistakenly configured with Administrative Distance 90 instead of 130.

show_commands.output:
Routing entry for 0.0.0.0/0, supernet
  Known via "static", distance 90, metric 0
  Routing Descriptor Blocks:
  * 198.51.100.2, via GigabitEthernet0/2

expected_fault: Floating static route configured with AD 90 (lower than OSPF AD 110).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Administrative distance of floating static route is set to 90, which is lower than OSPF (110). The router prefers the static backup link over the primary OSPF link.
evidence: show ip route shows distance 90 for static default route
fix_steps: Verify OSPF route enters RIB: show ip route

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Setting AD to 130 ensures static route only activates when OSPF fails.

title: Recursive Static Route Next-Hop Unresolvable
symptoms: Configured static route "ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.5.5.5" does not appear in "show ip route" table.
topology_notes: Next-hop IP 10.5.5.5 is not directly connected and has no route in R1 routing table.

show_commands.output: % Subnet not in table

expected_fault: Next-hop 10.5.5.5 cannot be resolved via any interface or route, so route is not installed in RIB.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Static route next-hop 10.5.5.5 is not reachable in the routing table. Cisco IOS will not install a static route into the RIB unless the next-hop IP resolves to an active outgoing interface.
evidence: show ip route 10.5.5.5 returns "Subnet not in table"
fix_steps: Correct the next-hop IP to the directly connected neighbor IP: R1(config)# no ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.5.5.5
Verify in RIB: show ip route 172.16.1.0

human_review.explanation: Accurate explanation of Cisco RIB installation rules.

title: OSPF Neighbor Adjacency Down — Area ID Mismatch
symptoms: R1 and R2 fail to form OSPF adjacency on link 10.0.0.0/30. "show ip ospf neighbor" returns empty. OSPF hello packets received but discarded.
topology_notes: R1 and R2 connected on GigabitEthernet0/0. R1 has network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0. R2 has network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 1.

show_commands.output:
GigabitEthernet0/0 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.0.0.1/30, Area 0, Attached via Interface Enable
  Process ID 1, Router ID 1.1.1.1, Network Type BROADCAST, Cost: 1
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40, Wait 40, Retransmit 5
-- No neighbors --

expected_fault: OSPF Area ID mismatch (Area 0 on R1 vs Area 1 on R2).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: OSPF Area ID mismatch on link 10.0.0.0/30. R1 is configured in Area 0 while R2 is configured in Area 1. OSPF requires matching Area IDs in Hello packets to establish Full adjacency.
evidence: R1 interface Gi0/0 is in Area 0
ai_diagnosis.next_command: show running-config | section router ospf on R2
fix_steps: Verify adjacency: show ip ospf neighbor

human_review.explanation: Verified area mismatch. Correcting R2 to Area 0 brought adjacency to FULL.

title: OSPF Hello/Dead Timer Mismatch on Point-to-Point Link
symptoms: OSPF adjacency continuously flaps or never forms between R1 and R2. Debug log: "OSPF: Dead timer mismatch on Gi0/1".
topology_notes: R1 Gi0/1 has "ip ospf hello-interval 10" and dead 40. R2 Gi0/1 was configured with "ip ospf hello-interval 30" and dead 120.

show_commands.output:
GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
  Internet Address 10.0.1.1/30, Area 0
  Timer intervals configured, Hello 10, Dead 40, Wait 40, Retransmit 5

expected_fault: Hello/Dead timer mismatch (10/40 on R1 vs 30/120 on R2).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: OSPF Hello and Dead intervals do not match on link Gi0/1. OSPF routers reject hello packets unless Hello and Dead timers match identically.
ai_diagnosis.next_command: show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 on R2
fix_steps: Align timers on R2: R2(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1

human_review.explanation: Timer alignment resolved the flapping adjacency immediately.

title: OSPF Stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE State (MTU Mismatch)
symptoms: OSPF neighbor state is stuck in EXSTART/EXCHANGE and never reaches FULL. Large database description (DBD) packets are dropped.
topology_notes: R1 Gi0/1 has default MTU 1500. R2 Gi0/1 was configured with "ip mtu 1400" for a tunnel overlay.

show_commands.output:
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
2.2.2.2           1   EXSTART/ -      00:00:33    10.0.2.2        GigabitEthernet0/1

GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
  Hardware is CN Gigabit Ethernet, address is 0001.9659.8601
  MTU 1500 bytes, BW 1000000 Kbit/sec, DLY 10 usec

expected_fault: Interface MTU mismatch (1500 on R1 vs 1400 on R2) causes DBD packets to fail exchange.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: OSPF Network Type mismatch (Broadcast vs Point-to-Point) causing DR/BDR election conflict.
fix_steps: Change network type to point-to-point: R1(config-if)# ip ospf network point-to-point

corrected_response.root_cause: MTU mismatch between R1 (MTU 1500) and R2 (MTU 1400). OSPF DBD packets larger than 1400 bytes are dropped by R2, locking the adjacency in EXSTART/EXCHANGE state.
fix_steps: Align MTU on R2: R2(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
Or ignore MTU mismatch: R2(config-if)# ip ospf mtu-ignore
Verify state reaches FULL: show ip ospf neighbor

human_review.explanation: AI REJECTION (Responsible AI): AI mistakenly diagnosed OSPF Network Type mismatch. An EXSTART stuck state is the textbook symptom of MTU mismatch during DBD packet exchange.

title: OSPF Passive Interface Blocking Adjacency on Core Uplink
symptoms: R1 fails to form OSPF relationship with Core R2. "show ip ospf neighbor" shows no adjacency on Gi0/0.
topology_notes: Administrator used "passive-interface default" under router ospf 1 and forgot to issue "no passive-interface Gi0/0".

show_commands.output:
router ospf 1
 router-id 1.1.1.1
 passive-interface default
 network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0

expected_fault: Gi0/0 is silenced by "passive-interface default" and missing "no passive-interface Gi0/0".

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: OSPF is suppressed on Gi0/0 due to "passive-interface default". Passive interfaces do not transmit OSPF Hello packets, preventing neighbor formation on the Core link.
fix_steps: Verify neighbor state: show ip ospf neighbor

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Re-enabling OSPF hellos on Gi0/0 formed adjacency immediately.

title: eBGP Multihop Missing on Loopback Peering Session
symptoms: eBGP session between R1 and R2 remains in "Idle" or "Active" state. TCP connection for BGP port 179 fails to establish.
topology_notes: R1 and R2 peer using loopback addresses (1.1.1.1 and 2.2.2.2). Default eBGP TTL is 1.

show_commands.output:
BGP router identifier 1.1.1.1, local AS number 65001
Neighbor        V           AS MsgRcvd MsgSent   TblVer  InQ OutQ Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
2.2.2.2         4        65002       0       0        1    0    0 00:15:22 Idle

router bgp 65001
 neighbor 2.2.2.2 remote-as 65002
 neighbor 2.2.2.2 update-source Loopback0

expected_fault: eBGP requires "neighbor 2.2.2.2 ebgp-multihop 2" when peering across loopbacks.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: eBGP peering is configured to loopback IP 2.2.2.2 without "ebgp-multihop". By default, eBGP packets have TTL=1 and are dropped by the receiving router when routed to a loopback interface.
evidence: show ip bgp summary shows 2.2.2.2 in Idle state

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Setting ebgp-multihop 2 allowed BGP SYN packets to establish TCP session.

title: BGP Route Not Advertised — Network Mask Mismatch
symptoms: Enterprise LAN subnet 10.10.0.0/24 is not being advertised to BGP neighbor. "show ip bgp" on R1 is empty for that prefix.
topology_notes: RIB has 10.10.0.0/24 directly connected. BGP config has "network 10.10.0.0 mask 255.0.0.0" (/8).

show_commands.output:
Routing entry for 10.10.0.0/24
  Known via "connected", distance 0, metric 0 (connected)
  * directly connected, via GigabitEthernet0/2

router bgp 65001
 network 10.10.0.0 mask 255.0.0.0
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 remote-as 100

expected_fault: BGP network command mask (255.0.0.0) does not match exact RIB prefix (255.255.255.0).

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: BGP neighbor session needs a soft reset (clear ip bgp * soft) to trigger outbound route refresh.
fix_steps: R1# clear ip bgp * soft out

corrected_response.root_cause: BGP network statement specifies classful /8 mask (255.0.0.0), but the routing table (RIB) contains an exact /24 (255.255.255.0). BGP strictly requires an exact match of prefix AND mask in the RIB to originate a route.
fix_steps: Verify prefix origin: show ip bgp 10.10.0.0/24

human_review.explanation: AI MISDIAGNOSIS (Responsible AI): AI recommended clearing BGP sessions. The fundamental issue is that BGP will never originate a route if the network statement mask does not match the RIB entry.

title: iBGP Learned Route Inaccessible (Next-Hop Unreachable)
symptoms: R3 learns external prefix 203.0.113.0/24 via iBGP from R1, but the route is not installed in R3 routing table. Route status is "valid" but not "best".
topology_notes: R1 learns prefix from eBGP with next-hop 198.51.100.1 and advertises to iBGP peer R3 without modifying the next-hop.

show_commands.output:
BGP routing table entry for 203.0.113.0/24, version 5

title: Inter-VLAN ACL Blocking HTTP Port 80 Traffic
symptoms: Clients can ping web server at 192.168.30.10, but web browser displays "Connection Timed Out" when loading http://192.168.30.10.

ACL permits eq 8080, but web traffic is on port 80

title: Standard ACL Placed Near Source Blocking All Outbound Traffic
symptoms: Sales PC 192.168.10.5 was intended to be blocked from accessing Server 192.168.30.50 only, but now cannot reach the Internet or any other subnet.
topology_notes: Admin configured standard ACL 1 "access-list 1 deny 192.168.10.5" and applied it inbound on Gi0/0 (Sales LAN gateway).

show_commands.output:
Standard IP access list 1
    10 deny 192.168.10.5
    20 permit any (340 matches)

interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip access-group 1 in

expected_fault: Standard ACL filters on source IP only and was placed near source, dropping all traffic from 192.168.10.5.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: AI Initial Diagnosis: ACL 1 rule order is incorrect or needs a permit statement added.
fix_steps: Add permit rule on top: access-list 1 permit any

checks.message: Standard ACL applied at source blocks all traffic

corrected_response.root_cause: Standard ACLs evaluate SOURCE address only. Applying Standard ACL 1 on the source gateway interface Gi0/0 filters ALL outbound traffic from 192.168.10.5. Filtering a specific destination requires an Extended ACL placed near the source.
fix_steps: Remove Standard ACL from Gi0/0: R1(config-if)# no ip access-group 1 in
Create Extended ACL: R1(config)# ip access-list extended 105
Apply Extended ACL on Gi0/0: R1(config)# interface Gi0/0

human_review.explanation: AI MISDIAGNOSIS (Responsible AI): AI suggested "permit any" in the standard ACL which would unblock everything. Cisco rule: Standard ACLs must be placed near destination; to filter source-to-destination traffic at the source interface, an Extended ACL is required.

title: NAT Overload Missing "overload" Keyword on Source List
symptoms: The first user to browse the web succeeds, but all subsequent users fail to connect to external sites.
topology_notes: Router R1 provides NAT between LAN Gi0/1 and WAN Gi0/0 (Public IP 203.0.113.1).

show_commands.output:
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip nat outside
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip nat inside

Pro Inside global      Inside local       Outside local      Outside global
--- 203.0.113.1        192.168.1.10       ---                ---

expected_fault: Static 1-to-1 dynamic NAT configured instead of PAT because "overload" keyword is omitted.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: The NAT translation statement "ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/0" is missing the "overload" keyword. Without overload, Cisco IOS performs 1-to-1 static NAT, locking the single public IP to the first host that transmits.
evidence: show ip nat translations shows single 1-to-1 binding
fix_steps: R1(config)# no ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload
Verify multiple translations: show ip nat translations

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Adding "overload" enabled PAT for all concurrent LAN sessions.

title: Lightweight AP CAPWAP Discovery Failure (Missing DHCP Option 43)
symptoms: Lightweight AP powers on, receives an IP address on management VLAN 100, but fails to join WLC. AP console logs: "Translating CISCO-CAPWAP-CONTROLLER... Failed to find WLC".
topology_notes: AP is on subnet 192.168.100.0/24. WLC is on 10.10.10.5. DHCP pool for VLAN 100 is missing Option 43 (or DNS entry CISCO-CAPWAP-CONTROLLER).

show_commands.output:
ip dhcp pool AP_MGMT
 network 192.168.100.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.100.1
 dns-server 10.10.10.2

expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing Option 43 hex string specifying WLC management IP 10.10.10.5.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Lightweight AP cannot discover the WLC across subnets because DHCP pool AP_MGMT lacks Option 43 (vendor-specific option pointing to WLC IP 10.10.10.5).
evidence: DHCP pool AP_MGMT has no option 43
AP console logs CAPWAP discovery timeout
fix_steps: R1(dhcp-config)# option 43 hex f1040a0a0a05 (f1: type, 04: length 4 bytes, 0a0a0a05: 10.10.10.5)
Reboot AP to trigger CAPWAP join

human_review.explanation: Configuring Option 43 in DHCP allowed LAP-101 to register with WLC.

title: STP Root Bridge Contention — Access Switch Winning Root Election
symptoms: Sub-optimal Layer 2 traffic paths across campus. All traffic hairpins through an access switch in the wiring closet. High CPU on access switch.
topology_notes: Core switch SW-Core has default STP priority 32768 (MAC 0001.c789.1111). Access switch SW-Access3 has default priority 32768 (MAC 0000.0c12.3456 - lower MAC won election).
expected_fault: STP priority was left at default (32768) on all switches, causing oldest access switch to win root bridge.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: All switches have default Spanning Tree priority (32768). Access switch SW-Access3 won the Root Bridge election due to having the lowest numerical MAC address, creating inefficient spanning-tree topology.
evidence: show spanning-tree root shows Root ID priority 32769 at 0000.0c12.3456 (Access switch)
fix_steps: Set Core as Primary Root: SW-Core(config)# spanning-tree vlan 1-4094 priority 4096
Set Distribution as Secondary: SW-Dist(config)# spanning-tree vlan 1-4094 priority 8192
Verify root location: show spanning-tree root

human_review.explanation: Accurate. Setting priority 4096 on Core switch established deterministic STP topology.

title: Sticky MAC Address Mismatch After PC Replacement
symptoms: IT technician replaced a defective desktop on Fa0/15. The new PC cannot obtain link or send packets.
topology_notes: Port Fa0/15 has static/sticky MAC address bound to the old PC MAC (0011.2233.4455).
expected_fault: Sticky MAC 0011.2233.4455 does not match the new replacement PC MAC address.

ai_diagnosis.root_cause: Port Fa0/15 has sticky MAC address 0011.2233.4455 hardcoded in running-config from the retired PC. The new PC has a different MAC address and is blocked by Port Security.
fix_steps: Clear old sticky MAC: SW1(config)# interface FastEthernet0/15
SW1(config-if)# no switchport port-security mac-address sticky 0011.2233.4455

human_review.explanation: Cleared old sticky MAC. New PC registered its MAC and came online immediately.
